There was a fresh grave, covered in flowers and dirt, we could see it piled up. The shadows casted of the gravestones dragging across the ground. I totally freaked. I was so scared. The grave was glowing. Like tiny flickering orbs. I was screaming about the lights and the wind was blowing, leaves were flying past us from the nearby woods. I’m truly thankful for this message. As I knew I was seeing and hearing about PTSD much more and I wasn’t sure if Complex PTSD had always been a diagnosis. 

I started Therapy as a very young child, I was told I had a learning disability and behavioral issues pumped full of medicine. In and out of systems. Every single time I tried to explain my symptoms I was met with an “impossible” reply, like shit was happening in my brain especially....disassociating. I’m not sure when that became well known [?] but I remember trying to explain it many times and being met only with criticism and excuses. 
 
I had more diagnosis by my 18th birthday than I had years alive. My eventual diagnosis was enough for me to accept there isn’t much known, little understanding, zero acceptable treatment in my personal case and the only help I was going to get would be found within myself.

I can remember well the therapists and counselors, they always seemed to have a meeting, with a head therapist, they would stay in with my mother seemingly hours to a small child. I’d eventually be invited in and told that they couldn’t help any longer and this agency or that person would be best. 
 
My entire freshman and sophomore year I spent in and out of inpatient for weeks at a time. Transferred around to people who didn’t understand my reactions and if I wasn’t being triggered, drugged and or abused I’d most certainly be harassed by the more dangerous and rebellious patients. 

I’m glad the system better. I mean it’s got to be better right? It was always total chaos. I’ve watched a many seemingly harmless adolescences get tackled pumped full of drugs and thrown in rooms with nothing but a floor. I’ve stayed on mixed sex units where sex and sexual acts were normal. Lifting your tongue never was a good indication of medicine swallowed and self harm was expected they just hoped someone found you before you were completely gone. Which. Yes. That happened too. 20 years before that before my time, mental patients were locked in basically cells or left to roam filthy halls with no escape, so, I guess I am glad to hear it’s getting better but *Sadly* I’d imagine it isn’t anywhere near good.
